4. Artificial intelligence: our commitments under EU law

VF Empire designs and builds artificial intelligence systems. We operate within the European Union and treat the European regulatory framework for AI as an engineering specification.

4.1 The EU Artificial Intelligence Act

Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council (the “EU AI Act”) establishes a harmonised, risk-based legal framework for artificial intelligence in the Union. VF Empire commits to the following in the design, development and delivery of its systems:

  • Prohibited practices (Article 5). We do not design, build or deploy AI systems for practices prohibited by the EU AI Act, including manipulative or exploitative techniques causing significant harm, social scoring by or for public authorities, untargeted scraping of facial images for recognition databases, emotion recognition in workplaces or educational institutions (outside legal exemptions), or real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces outside the narrow exceptions provided by law.
  • Risk classification. Every system programme we undertake is assessed against the AI Act’s risk categories before build. Where a commissioned system would qualify as a high-risk AI system (Annex III), we engineer to the corresponding requirements: risk management systems (Article 9), data governance (Article 10), technical documentation (Article 11), record-keeping and logging (Article 12), transparency to deployers (Article 13), human oversight (Article 14), and accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity (Article 15).
  • Human oversight by architecture. VF systems are built around gates: outputs are checked against evidence, and decision authority remains with accountable humans. Supervised autonomy is our default engineering posture, not an optional extra.
  • Transparency (Article 50). Where our systems interact directly with natural persons, they are designed to disclose that the person is interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from context. Where our systems generate or manipulate synthetic content, we support machine-readable marking of such content in accordance with the Act.
  • General-purpose AI models. VF Empire primarily integrates and orchestrates open-source and third-party models rather than placing its own general-purpose AI models on the Union market. Where obligations for providers or deployers of general-purpose AI models (Chapter V) apply to an engagement, they are addressed in the engagement’s technical documentation.
  • AI literacy (Article 4). Our AI Training Centre programmes are designed to advance the AI literacy of the people who operate, deploy and are affected by AI systems.

4.2 Data protection

Our systems are engineered local-first: models, data and controls are designed to run on infrastructure controlled by the system’s owner. Processing of personal data by VF Empire is governed by Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (“GDPR”) and Maltese data protection law, as described in our Privacy Policy. Where VF acts as a processor for a client, a data processing agreement pursuant to Article 28 GDPR forms part of the engagement.

4.3 No guarantee of regulatory outcomes

Statements on this Site about regulatory compliance describe our engineering commitments and methodology. They are not legal advice to you, and they do not guarantee that any particular deployment by a client (whose context, data and use case we may not control) will satisfy the legal obligations that apply to that client. Responsibility for a deployer’s obligations under the EU AI Act, GDPR and other applicable law rests with the deployer.

15. Permanence Guarantee

The Permanence Guarantee is a binding commitment that a VF Empire product, once purchased, remains usable and open to its buyers even if VF Empire discontinues it. This section defines the trigger, the timeline and the specific obligations. A plain-language summary is published at vfempire.com/permanence-guarantee; where the summary and this section conflict, this section prevails.

15.1 Trigger

The Guarantee is invoked when any of the following occurs:

  1. VF Empire publicly announces the end of life of a product;
  2. VF Empire ceases to distribute installers of a product, and ceases to accept new purchases of that product, for more than 120 consecutive days without a published maintenance-mode statement covering the interval;
  3. VF Empire is dissolved, liquidated or wound up; or is acquired by a party that within 90 days of the acquisition announces the discontinuation of a product covered by these Terms, or removes such a product from public sale.

15.2 Obligations on trigger

Within 90 days of the trigger occurring, VF Empire (or its liquidator, administrator or successor) shall:

  1. release the full source code of the affected product under the Apache License, Version 2.0 or a compatible OSI-approved permissive licence, published to a public code repository;
  2. publish the product's library, catalogue or data format specification to the same repository or to a public specification host, in sufficient detail for a competent third party to write an interoperable implementation;
  3. mirror the last-shipped installer and its build inputs to at least one independent transparency log (for example Software Heritage or the Internet Archive Wayback Machine);
  4. ensure the Ed25519 public key used to sign the affected product's licences and updates remains valid, and refrain from revoking or invalidating that key.

15.3 No dependency on VF services

Products covered by this section are engineered so that continued use requires no online activation, no periodic licence check, and no continued availability of VF Empire's servers. This is a design commitment applied product by product and confirmed in each product's public security posture.

15.4 Scope

The Guarantee applies to any product sold by VF Empire to a consumer or business under a perpetual, one-off or lifetime licence. It does not apply to services expressly sold on a subscription-only basis (consulting engagements, hosted APIs), except that any client work delivered under section 6 (Commissioned systems) remains subject to the delivery contract governing that engagement.

15.5 Enforcement

This section is a contractual undertaking of VF Empire Corp Ltd, enforceable by any purchaser of the affected product in accordance with section 14 (Governing law and jurisdiction).

16. Product warranties

Where a product is sold by VF Empire under these Terms, the following warranties apply from the first day of the first paid subscription period or from the date of first paid activation, whichever is earlier. These warranties are in addition to, and do not displace, statutory rights held by a consumer under Maltese law or under mandatory law of the consumer's EU country of habitual residence.

16.1 Privacy-breach warranty

A "material privacy breach" is a confirmed incident in which user data that a product's public documentation stated would not be accessible to VF Empire, would not leave the user's own hardware, or would remain encrypted at rest end to end, becomes accessible to VF Empire, to a third party, or is exfiltrated in plaintext, as a result of a flaw in the product, in its distributed dependencies, or in VF Empire's operational practice.

On confirmation of a material privacy breach affecting a paying customer, VF Empire shall:

  1. refund that customer the full price of their current subscription period; or, for a one-off or lifetime licence, refund a proportion of the licence price equal to the fraction of the calendar year remaining from the date of confirmation; whichever refund is higher applies;
  2. publish a written post-mortem within five business days of confirmation, at vfempire.com or a successor domain, disclosing the incident timeline, the root cause, the scope of user data affected, the remediation applied, and the concrete change made to prevent recurrence.

16.2 Confirmation

"Confirmation" means an internal determination by VF Empire that the incident occurred; or a determination by a national data-protection authority, a court of competent jurisdiction, or an independent security researcher acting in good faith with reproducible evidence.

16.3 Coordinated disclosure preserved

Nothing in section 16.1 requires disclosure of information whose immediate publication would enable further exploitation of an unpatched vulnerability. VF Empire may withhold specific technical detail from the five-business-day post-mortem for coordinated disclosure, provided the incident timeline, cause class, scope and remediation summary are published on time. Withheld technical detail shall be published within a further 30 days.

16.4 Enforcement

This section is enforceable in accordance with section 14 (Governing law and jurisdiction). Refund obligations may be exercised by ordinary contract-law remedies; failure to publish the post-mortem within the time specified in section 16.1 is itself a breach of these Terms.
